title: The Dead Sea Scrolls — Biblical and Non-Biblical Scrolls, Abegg–Bowley–Cook Transcriptions (ETCBC Text-Fabric)
edition: M.G. Abegg, Jr., J.E. Bowley, E.M. Cook, electronic transcriptions with morphological tagging (1995-2015), prepared for the Brill Dead Sea Scrolls Concordances; readings primarily follow DJD (Oxford: Clarendon, 1955-) with editors' own reconstructions where editions do not supply them; converted to Text-Fabric by J. Jacobs, M. Naaijer, D. Roorda (CACCHT project, ETCBC)

origin.transport: git sparse checkout at pinned commit; Transport D, No-Double-Draw: no paid API invoked

language: Hebrew; Aramaic (feature 'lang' distinguishes; Paleo-Hebrew and Greek script signs flagged via 'script')

license.payload: CC BY-NC 4.0 — declared at the file in every Text-Fabric feature header (@license, @licenseUrl), with @createdBy=Abegg/Bowley/Cook and @source=Martin Abegg's data files, personal communication. Repo-level MIT covers packaging/software only.
license.record: CC-BY-4.0 applies to this seat record and the alexanarch record text only, NOT to the corpus payload. The payload license is BY-NC and is carried forward unmodified. First NC-licensed seat in the library; redistribution here is non-commercial.
license.chain_note: Ancient texts public domain. Transcription/reconstruction layer created by Abegg, Bowley and Cook and provided by Abegg personally to CACCHT (documented in repo about.md and in the .tf headers); the license is therefore declared by the parties holding the transcription rights - the structural opposite of a third-party relicensing defect. Caveat recorded honestly: Qimron v. Shanks (Israel) held a scholar's scroll reconstruction copyrightable to the reconstructor; readings herein that follow Qimron's published editions rest on the ground that following an edition's readings is not copying its protected expression. The principal reconstructors are the grantors here.
license.provenance_event: The corpus enters the archive through the hand that liberated it: Abegg's 1991 reconstruction of the scrolls from the Brill concordance broke a forty-year publication monopoly. @source=Martin Abegg's data files, personal communication.

scope: Both biblical (265 scrolls, incl. biblical=2 tefillin/mezuzot class) and non-biblical (735 scrolls + composites incl. CD). Ruled 2026-08-22: biblical scrolls are witnesses, not duplicates of the Leningrad seat (EA-CORPORA-01/09); seated for the comparative-witness program.
reconstructions: Included and flagged, per ruling 2026-08-22. Flat layer wraps reconstructed sign-runs in [square brackets] driven by the 'rec' feature, single running state per line (edition convention). Uncertainty (unc), corrections (cor), alternates (alt), removals (rem) preserved in original/ TF features, not carried into the flat layer.
encoding_conventions: Abegg source conventions preserved: ׳ = morpheme/suffix boundary marker; ׃ = source punctuation mark; ε = placeholder/empty-sign glyph in the source data; ╱ = source line marker. Graphic-word spacing reconstructed from the sign-level 'after' feature.
normalization: tf/1.9 sign stream -> flat ref-tagged lines '<scroll> <fragment/column>:<line>\t<text>' via glyph+punc+after per sign with rec-bracketing. 52,878 lines: biblical.txt 16,286; nonbiblical.txt 36,592.
